newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: U.S. declines lead Australian stocks lower at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. declines lead Australian stocks lower at open.

text.p: The Australian share market started the week 0.45 percent weaker following Friday's U.S. declines.
"We're coming down purely on the back of Wall Street. Commodities didn't do much," one Sydney-based broker said.
At 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index had lost 12.8 points to 2,714.7 in low turnover of A$40.79 million.
Dealers said activity was hampered by the bank holiday in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, with many institutional players absent from the market.
Bellwether BHP shed nine cents to A$17.92, while Rio Tinto fell 9.3 cents A$20.70 and WMC lost three cents to A$7.61.
The banks fell more than the overall market, with the sector index 0.6 percent weaker in early trade.
"We're having some impact from bond yields," said David Perry of Austock Brokers in Melbourne.
ANZ fell seven cents to A$10.63 and Westpac Banking eight cents to A$8.54. National Australia Bank slid six cents to A$19.45.
Dealers said investors had started to look ahead to the string of full-year results coming up in the next few weeks.

News Corp initially rose two cents to A$6.15, but soon fell back to trade two cents down at A$6.11 after newspaper reports that analysts have revised downwards their 1996/97 year net profit forecasts for the media and entertainment giant.
Coca-Cola Amatil fell 18 cents to A$16.07 ahead of its first-half profit announcement on Wednesday.
Brokers said the market was not expecting Tuesday's Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) meeting to produce much news after last week's 0.5 percentage point interest rate cut to 5.0 percent.
